subject: Hosted API evaluation — quickstart, endpoints & rate limits
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Thanks — next steps on Hosted API evaluation

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for your time earlier today — great to learn more about FinLytics' ingestion pipeline and the latency/cost targets you mentioned for real-time summarization (p95 < 450ms, target token cost ~$0.002/token). Per our conversation, it sounds like you want to start with Hosted API for a quickproof/POC and then evaluate Dedicated if throughput or isolation needs increase.

Recap / proposed next steps:
- Quickstart: I can provision an evaluation API key and a sample dataset walkthrough so your engineers can hit the /v1/chat/completions endpoint and test streaming.
- Rate limits: default eval limits are conservative (see details below) but we can temporarily raise them for your test window.
- Data & security: Redwood Hosted does not use customer request data to train models; we have SOC 2 and can provide an evidence packet.
- Ops follow-up: Marissa (cc'd) will help with the quickstart and performance tuning (batching/kv-caching suggestions).

If that sounds right, I will: 1) generate an eval key, 2) share the quickstart guide and example cURL/snippets, and 3) coordinate a 30-min handoff with Marissa next week.

One question: for the POC, do you expect to use streaming tokens heavily (live UI) or batched summarization jobs? That will help us set the right rate-limit bump.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0172

Attachment: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@finlytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — next steps on Hosted API evaluation

Hi Aditya — thanks for the clear recap.

We'd like to start with Hosted API. A few answers and questions:
- Use case: live UI summarization for support agents (streaming preferred) with a fallback batched job for long transcripts.
- Expected load for POC: ~8 concurrent users to start, peaking ~40 concurrent during load test. Average request size ~600 tokens, typical responses ~120 tokens.
- Security: procurement will want the SOC2 evidence and an outline of retention & logging (we cannot keep customer PII).
- Rate limits: please share the current default and what an eval bump looks like (both requests/sec and tokens/min).

Also copying procurement to coordinate any paperwork: procurement@finlytics.com

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Product | FinLytics
samira.khan@finlytics.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks — next steps on Hosted API evaluation

Hi Samira — perfect, thanks for the details.

Answers inline:
- Streaming: Hosted streaming is fully supported via the /v1/chat/completions streaming mode. Marissa will share a sample WebSocket/Server-Sent-Events snippet in the quickstart.
- Default eval rate limits: 60 requests/minute and 50,000 tokens/minute on the default evaluation tier. That maps roughly to the POC numbers you gave (8–40 concurrency).
- Eval bump: for a 2-week eval we can provision a temporary bump to 300 requests/minute and 250,000 tokens/minute. If you need higher sustained throughput we can move you to Dedicated capacity.
- Data retention & security: Hosted request logs are retained by default for 30 days for debugging; we can configure a shorter window (e.g., 7 days) for your account or disable request logging for particular routes. We are SOC 2 Type II; I'll attach the evidence packet (redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf includes the next steps to request the full pack).

Next steps I can take now:
1) Generate an eval API key scoped to FinLytics and enable the temporary rate-limit bump for your test window (let me know preferred start date).
2) Marissa to run a 30-min handoff next Tue/Wed to walk through the quickstart and sample scripts (she can also suggest batching/kv-cache settings for 600-token inputs).
3) I'll share the SOW draft for procurement to review (attached).

Proposed start for the eval bump: Monday, 9 Mar 2026. Is that workable?

Thanks — Marissa & Dev, can you pick this up for the quickstart and workload tuning?

Best,
Aditya
